solution: The opening section defines the term almost in the words of the stem: "There are many independent nations in the world like India... These independent States also enter into treaties with each other. A system of all these independent, sovereign States comes up. We call it international system." 'Political system' and 'social system' are used in the chapter for structures inside a country, not for the community of sovereign States.

The chapter's phrase 'main responsibility ... to avoid war' appears verbatim about the League of Nations ("The main responsibility of the League of Nations was understood to be to avoid war"), and it states the same core duty for its successor in the Post-Cold War World section: "The responsibility of the United Nations has increased. The United Nations now had to take more concrete steps to maintain global peace and security." Disarmament and decolonisation are treated in the chapter as activities/effects of the Cold War period rather than the UN's stated main responsibility, and improving other nations' economies is nowhere assigned to the UN — so (a) is the main responsibility and (b)/(c)/(d) are true-but-not-what-was-asked.

The 'Post-Cold War World' section opens: "The Cold War came to an end with the disintegration of the Soviet Russia, which till then had been a super power." The other options are events of the wrong direction or period — the United Nations and the military organisations (NATO, Warsaw Pact) were created at the START of the Cold War, and the Cuban Missile Crisis (1962) is described in the chapter as "an important event in the cold war period", i.e. during it, not its end.
